note: Manually curated from public news and institutional sources (not automated). Coordinates and radii are approximate — they mark a general area, not an exact boundary. Absence from this list does NOT mean an area is free of enforcement; it means it wasn't specifically documented in the sources checked. enforcement_level reflects reported real-world patrol/fine activity, which is a different question from whether camping is legally banned there (most of Greece is, nationally, since Law 5170/2025 and 5209/2025). Entries are scoped as tightly as the sourcing allows — a single dated incident at a named beach gets a small radius around that beach, not the whole surrounding region, so an unrelated beach 50km away doesn't inherit the same warning.

hotspots.name: Kavourotrypes & Sithonia peninsula beaches (Halkidiki)
hotspots.note: Repeated, dated arrests for illegal camping at Kavourotrypes specifically (2017, 2018), and local press reporting the 2025 national law (5170/2025, refined by 5209/2025) being actively enforced against camper vans across the peninsula's beaches more broadly.

hotspots.name: Elaia beach & pine forest, Messinia (Neda river mouth)
hotspots.note: A recurring, specific enforcement site, not a one-off: police raids with mass arrests for illegal camping at this exact beach/forest in 2023 (13 arrests), 2025 (the first arrests made anywhere under the new law), and again in 2026 (18 arrests, also involving drugs and unlicensed radio equipment). This is a named beach 10km north of Kyparissia, distinct from the Kyparissia Bay/Voidokilia entry below.

hotspots.name: Thapsa beach, Kymi, Evia
hotspots.note: Heavy, widely-reported fines against free campers at this specific beach in June 2024, after complaints from locals about overcrowding. Coordinates are an estimate from descriptive routing (reached via dirt road south of Kymi, past Konistres/Maletianoi/Tsilaro) rather than a confirmed GPS pin — verify the exact spot before relying on this radius.

hotspots.name: Zakynthos National Marine Park (Laganas Bay: Sekania, Dafni, Gerakas)
hotspots.note: Sea-turtle nesting beaches patrolled directly by National Marine Park rangers; camping and fires are explicitly banned and fines are enforced. Sekania beach is accessible only by licensed boat or ranger escort.

hotspots.name: Elafonisi / Balos / Preveli (Crete)
hotspots.note: Natura 2000 dune/lagoon systems historically popular with backpacker tent camping. Rangers are now present in season, camping and fires are banned, and €300 fines are reported as increasingly enforced.

hotspots.name: Kyparissia Bay / Voidokilia / Gialova Lagoon (Messinia)
hotspots.note: Legally protected Natura 2000 loggerhead turtle nesting habitat, with camping banned under a 2018 presidential decree — but conservation groups (MEDASSET, 2023 Bern Convention review) report that enforcement of that decree has been largely absent. Legally off-limits and ecologically sensitive either way; just don't mistake low patrol activity for it being allowed.
